newsitem.title: USA: Clinton requests $265 billion for defense.
newsitem.headline: Clinton requests $265 billion for defense.

text.p: President Clinton sought $265 billion in defense spending authority Thursday as part of his budget plan, including a portion of a $3.5 billion payment to keep U.S. troops in Bosnia another 18 months.
The defense spending request in Clinton's $1.69 trillion budget for fiscal 1998 that begins Oct. 1, seems certain to spark a fight with a Republican-controlled Congress that wanted $6.8 billion more.
The $265 billion request compares to defense spending authority of $262 billion in fiscal 1997.

Defense officials told reporters they also expected protests over the size of the Bosnia request, $1.5 billion in the budget plus an additional $2 billion to be asked for separately, though Congress seldom rejects money for troops already committed abroad.

Congress approved U.S. troops for the NATO peacekeeping operation in Bosnia for one year, ending last month. But Clinton and allied leaders decided to keep troops there 18 months more to give peace a better chance to last.
Legislators including Sen. Dan Coats, an Indiana Republican, criticized Clinton for making the commitment without Congress's advance approval but Coats predicted Congress would go along.

The Republican-controlled Congress has added billions of dollars to each of Clinton's defense requests, accusing Clinton of cuts jeopardizing military readiness, and is likely to add money again this year.
Congress had allotted $272 billion for defense for next year in the budget resolution it approved last year, $6.8 billion more than Clinton's new request.
Defense spending authority includes additional money for projects that will continue over several years.
The defense authority request for 1998 is over $13 billion higher that the less-inclusive "military authority" figure contained in the summary budget tables.
Defense outlays reflect only the money spent in a particular year and that figure can be higher or lower than authority, depending on what items that money is being spent on.
Clinton's proposed fiscal 1998 outlays total $259 billion compared to $267 billion in 1997.
Clinton's new defense request includes:

-- $3.5 billion for anti-missile defenses that would continue only to develop a U.S. missile defense that could be built by 2003 rather that commit to the construction as congressional Republicans want. But in a concession to the legislators, it would speed up delivery of advanced battlefield anti-missiles like those used in the Gulf War.
-- $3 billion for three Aegis destroyers built by Bath Iron Works and Ingalls Shipbuilding.
-- $3 billion for development of a new attack submarine by General Dynamics Electric Boat Division and the Newport News Shipbuilding and Drydock Co.
-- $2.5 billion for 20 advanced Navy F/A-18E/F fighter-bombers built by McDonnell Douglas Corp.
-- $2.4 billion for nine more C-17 combat transport planes built by McDonnell Douglas.
-- $2.2 billion for developmnent of a new Air Force F-22 radar-evading stealth fighter plane by Lockheed Martin and Boeing.
-- A 2.8 percent military pay raise.
